Risk call on ARMY: **Refuse at any size** is my recommendation, but if the desk overrides, the most conservative terms are below.

Reasons to refuse: the 30-minute return is +3082% (31.8x) with a 12.6% drawdown from the high, so the entry is far from the launch price and most of the move is already priced in. The curve shows a launch bot present and top-3 holders at 38% of the curve. The 15-minute window had net flow of +335 SOL, but sellers (322) are well short of buyers (1,505), which reads like a late-stage chase rather than a healthy base. Pool depth of ~564 SOL is adequate, so slippage is not the binding constraint.

If overridden: $5 ticket, 20% stop, 15-minute max hold, exit on any break of the recent high.
memos.scout:
The case for buying ARMY now is real but thinner than the headline return suggests.

Demand is broad: 1,505 buyers and about 999 SOL bought in the last 15 minutes, net flow of +335 SOL, and 251 non-agent buyers in the first two minutes after graduation. The top-5 buyer share is 11%, and the top-3 holder share is 38%, not extreme for this type. The class is ORGANIC, with no airdrop dump, and the coin sits about 12.6% off its 30-minute high, so it has already absorbed some selling without collapsing.

The risks are concrete. Sellers are 322 against 1,505 buyers, and sell-to-buy in the launch window was 1.09, meaning early sellers matched early buyers. The 4.4x return in 15 minutes means much of the move is already priced in, and a 12.6% pullback is common before a further leg or a reversal. Pool depth of 563 SOL is adequate for a $20 ticket. The bundle share of 11.5% and a launch bot are worth noting.

I can make a honest case for a small position, but the base rates say most coins this age lose money on a random entry, and this one is up 32x in 30 minutes. Verdict: a marginal buy at best, not a strong one.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is a distribution into the dip. The coin has returned about 32x in 30 minutes and 4.4x in the last 15, so early holders have large gains to take. Sellers already outnumber buyers in the first two minutes after graduation (sell-to-buy ratio 1.087), and the price is already 12.6% off its 30-minute high. Pool depth is only 563.57 SOL, so a $20 round trip with 1.4-5.1% costs plus impact can easily absorb a modest move. Top-3 holders control 38.4% of the curve, and the 11.5% bundle share suggests coordinated early buying. Skip this one.
